# HTML images

READMEs often write images as `<img>` tags, to set a width or to put them in a table.

An `<img>` on its own line is a figure, and `width` limits its size:

<img src="images/landscape.png" alt="Sunset over the bay" width="320">

Centered with a paragraph tag, as many READMEs do:

<p align="center">
  <img src="images/tree.png" alt="A tall tree" width="160">
</p>

Screenshots in a table are drawn in their cells:

| Wide | Tall |
|---|---|
| <img src="images/landscape.png" alt="Sunset over the bay" width="240"> | <img src="images/tree.png" alt="A tall tree" width="120"> |

Inside a sentence, like this <img src="images/icon.png" alt="badge" width="16"> one, an `<img>` stays a text chip.

Other HTML is left alone: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>.
